finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. Any client can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs, including internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata), localhost services and private-network hosts. The response body is reflected back, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.source: HTTP GET /rss, query parameter params[:u], controlled by any unauthenticated client

trace.note: GET /rss route handler; the request is unauthenticated
params[:u] is passed unvalidated to URI.open, which performs the outbound request, and .read fetches the body
The first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-range blocking and no authentication on this route. open-uri also follows redirects, so even a filter on the initial host would not hold. The TRUSTED allowlist on line 5 is applied only in /trusted, not here.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes unvalidated params[:u] to URI.open(...).read and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes, with no auth or allowlist on /rss (the TRUSTED check at app.rb:14 only guards /trusted).
